product_title: The Friendly Swede (TM) 23 Items Accessories Bundle Kit for Apple iPod touch 8GB 32GB 64GB (2011 New 4th Generation) 4 4G in Retail Packaging
review_headline: Huge Set, Perfect for Younger Kids and Moderate Use
review_body:
Really, how can you beat the price on this set. There is no need to reiterate all the stuff that comes with it but it really does. I have to say that you can't expect everything to be in top quality condition. Some of it is mediocre. But everything is pretty good. My daughter has an iPod Touch 4th generation and had a blast going through everything and playing around. She loves swapping out all the cases and using the retractable charging cable. The earbuds are okay, they have some static and don't seem to be too even in each ear so I'm sure they won't last a long time. The fish cable holder is cute and the belt clip holster is what made her the happiest. The styluses are metal and have a cord to keep them plugged into the headphone jack so that you always have one handy. The screen protectors fit but we quickly took them off. My daughter didn't like the feel of them - although that was not the fault of the screen protectors.

A note about the cases that did bother my daughter - they were very hard to get on initially but softened up a little with use. However, they are not cut well enough to dock the iPod in a dock and charge it properly. They seem to hold it just a little out of full contact although with some playing around, I was able to get it to sit properly.

So for the price, for a younger child or the budget conscious person, this is a set packed with opportunities.

I was provided a set for evaluation and review.

product_title: DEH-X6600BT - Pioneer In-Dash CD/MP3/WMA Car Stereo Receiver with Bluetooth, iPhone/iPod USB Support, Android Media Access, and Pandora Ready
review_headline: Great Price For Everything This Receiver Comes with
review_body:
I have been using this receiver for about a week now. I am honestly pretty impressed with its capabilities compared to my old Sony receiver. The only thing I don't like about it is that this receiver is not very user friendly. I had to toy around with audio adjustments for maybe over an hour to finally get it to where I like it. If you know what all the audio adjustments mean, then that shouldn't be a problem for you. It's very easy to increase the bass, but adjusting the highs was my issue. I listen to a lot of rock and metal, so I didn't want to overwhelm the bass to where I couldn't hear the vocals or guitar.

This is definitely a great upgrade. The Bluetooth works great! I like it so much better than the pain in the butt auxiliary cable. It was very easy to set-up the Bluetooth. Now every time I turn on my truck, it automatically connects to my phone if the Bluetooth is on, and my music will start playing even without touching my phone (Galaxy SIII). The only thing I don't like about that, though, is that the song will start over from the beginning instead of playing where it left off. That makes me tempted to change the song so i don't have to hear the beginning again. Also, if you're wondering how far the Bluetooth reaches from the receiver before it starts not wanting to read your phone, I calculated it to be about 5-6 feet from the receiver.

The light effect is pretty cool as well if you're also wondering. You can keep the lights one color of your choice, or you can have it scan through all of the colors for a light-changing effect while you're driving. Or you can also make the lights change color quickly if you're really in a party mode!

Overall; Great product. I have now officially made myself a Pioneer fan. Any of my future vehicles, or friends' vehicles will now be recommended Pioneer product. I hope this review helps, because it would have helped me in my decision to decide on this thing before I spent an hour researchingit.

review_body:
I have had other Bluetooth speakers before. They were pretty good. I thought I was listening to great sound until I received Sentey B-treck S8 Bluetooth Speaker! It has been simply amazing from the time opened it! The speaker comes with a USB cord for charging. It will need an adapter be plugged into a wall or just plug it into your computer. The speaker itself is high quality. It has a soft rubber feel which is unique. The speakers go all around it unlike the ones I've had in the past. It doesn't have any buttons to operate. The speaker is touch sensitive. There is a power switch on the back along with USB and AUX cords slots. What surprised me the most? The sound quality is unlike no other! It is ridiculously loud! When listening through wireless connection, it will blow you out of the room with the sound. It lets you know when you have reached top sound by a simple beep. The sound is crystal clear. You can call and receive phone calls from it,too. As always, you can skip or go back to any music while playing just a touch of the top touch sensitive key. They do have a slight delay, but it's not enough to worry over. This has been one of my favorite speakers from the beginning of tearing it out of the packaging after receiving it with a discount. It has made my music experience a lot better. I am going to be enjoying it with times to come!

product_title: MP3 Player
review_headline: Great Price For A Great Refurbished Clip Zip
review_body:
This is a great MP3 player and perhaps has the best capacity, sound and functionality in this price range.

I just copy album folders and playlists to it and they're listed. I copy audiobook chapters to their folder and they're listed. It's simple and I don't even use the sync software.

The solid state memory makes it great for exercise. No issues with small impacts. I've dropped mine several times.

However, beware of rain or water getting under the buttons. Drying can bring it back, but best to avoid direct rain, etc. My first one did not come back, however, after it met the ocean. Salt corrosion won't go away.

Two things to know:

1. A common issue is it not being recognized by the computer when plugged into the USB port. Make sure settings>>system settings>>USB Mode is set to MTC. This resolves this issue most of the time.

2. Occasionally this player seems to die, not turn on even when you know it's charged. A reset is simply holding the power button down for an extended period of time, 20+ seconds, and releasing. This resolves this issue most of the time.

Outside of rain and water issues, this has been a dependable toy. The sound is also excellent and FAR better than cheapos in this field. Consider investing in a pair of better earbuds to enjoy the bass this little guy can put out. Those also can be had for under $10 if you search Amazon for feedback.

Enjoy!

product_title: Omaker M2 Bluetooth 4.0 Hi-Fi Speaker BoomBox Brushed Aluminium Portable NFC Speaker,Wireless Stereo bluetooth Speaker with Super-Sized 14W Driver
review_headline: Excellent audio from an attractive portable speaker
review_body:
[[VIDEOID:moF63JH8W9BHE9]]I've listened to a lot of Bluetooth speakers, and most of them had acceptable audio quality, but the Omaker M2 wireless stereo speaker is one of the best ones that I've heard. Unlike smaller cube-shaped portable speakers, the M2 has true stereophonic sound with clear channel separation, but it's small enough (7.3\\"x3.1\\"x2\\") and light enough (24.5 ounces) to be considered portable. With its matte black brushed aluminum case and black grill cloth, the speaker is attractive enough to have a place in a living room or den, but it appears to be durable enough for travel in a backpack too.

The M2 has a maximum audio output of 14 watts (7 watts each channel). That's enough sound to fill any room in most homes. I checked the speaker's sound quality with one of my music playlists. The audio was clean, vocals were very clear, and the bass was just heavy enough for my liking.

The M2 paired quickly with my Samsung Galaxy Tab 3 as device \\"OMAKER M2\\" with no code required. The Bluetooth range and stability were good, with solid performance to at least 30 feet on a line of sight. With a couple of walls between the speaker and the source, there were intermittent dropouts at distances of 25-30 feet.

The speaker has a control for play/pause, and combined controls for volume and tracks (if you're running a playlist with tracks). For using as a hands-free device when the M2 is paired with a cellphone, there's a button for answering and ending a call, and a microphone behind the grill cloth. I also connected the M2 to the audio jack of my tablet with an audio cable (included), and the sound was equally good. Rubber feet on the base of the speaker help to keep it in place on whatever surface you place it, a nice feature that also prevents scratching of your furniture. The speaker has a bottom-mounted carrying strap. That's a clever feature, since the strap doesn't show when the M2 is on a table, but it's there when you need to pick up the speaker.

The speaker has a built-in rechargeable 2000mAh battery, one of the higher-capacity batteries that I've seen in a portable Bluetooth speaker. The user's guide indicates that the battery is good for around 8 hours of play. I tested that by charging the M2's battery, then I started streaming music from iHeartRadio. After 12½ hours of playing at medium volume, I couldn't even get the low battery light, so suffice to say the M2 has great battery life. To recharge the battery, a 5V/1A (max) charger is recommended. A USB charging cable is included. The charging cable is an unusual design with three plugs - USB, micro USB, and 3.5mm audio plug. It serves as both a charging cable and an audio cable.

I was very impressed with the Omaker M2 speaker. It's attractive enough for use in your home or office, the audio quality is very good, and it's one of the few portable Bluetooth speakers I've seen that has true stereophonic sound with channel separation.

product_title: EC TECHNOLOGY? New design Backup External Battery Pack and Charger (Power Bank) with flashlight
review_body:
Bought this for long day trips when either I don't have access to a wall charger or when I'm too on-the-move to sit and wait for my phone to charge.
The overall verdict: awesome. This does what it's supposed to do and it does it well.
The light is a nice added feature, too. The cable that comes with it is nifty in that the end is interchangeable for different devices. Need micro USB for you device? Just swap the end piece. Want to charge your Iphone? Just swap the end piece. All the while you use only one cable. It's nice because you don't have to carry all of the separate charging cables with you. In theory, this is a great idea. One downside to that, I guess, is that you have to keep track of all the individual ends (good thing it comes with a nice quality bag for them and the battery).

The largest CON about this product, however, is that the connection between the cable and the different ends on it isn't perfect, which means no juice gets to your device. For example, I had my phone plugged in for about 2 hours (it takes roughly 1.5 hours to fully charge my dead Iphone 4), but the connection between the cable and the end piece apparently wasn't tight because my phone was only at about 15%. Needless to say, I was disappointed. So I just use my actual phone charging cable instead and it works fine

tltr / LONG STORY SHORT - This is worth the money, just don't use the cable that comes with it (only use the appropriate charging cables for your devices)

TIP: you may find that this will not fully charge your phone if you just plug it in. But if you turn your phone to "airplane mode" (or power it off altogether) before you plug it in, it will charge MUCH more quickly. :)

product_title: Generic Car Dashboard Video Camera Vehicle Video Accident Recorder (2.0" 1080P)
review_headline: This is not a good alternative to a good quality dash cam
review_body:
I purchased this to cover myself in the event of a driving incident or accident leading to a \\"he said, she said\\" statement when the authorities arrive.

My job in the service industry requires me to drive 25,000 a year in heavy city traffic. I witness numerous accidents and road rage and to this point, have avoided all of them.

I gave this product one star because the build quality and mount seem decent.

My camera arrived completely discharged. Not knowing if this is normal because the directions are microscopic and unreadable, I charged it overnight.
The next day I still only had one bar out of three on the battery indicator. This gave me roughly 3 minutes of tinkering before it shut down.

I fumbled with it until it powered up and automatically started recording while plugged into the cigarette lighter and auto-powered down when unplugged with no motion triggers for a minute or so. (I have over 10 years experience in the CCTV industry programming 100's of different DVR products)

I mounted it in my car but while addressing the best video angle was very disappointed. The field of view is very narrow. It barely covered my hood. How is that going to help me? I would need three of these to cover enough to capture what was going on in the left/right periphery.

The video quality was pretty good but the camera would stop recording until I powered it down and back up again. It would record for part of the day and need to be power cycled again. This was very random and was not related to the auto-shutdown or motion recording. I also verified the loop record was set properly. I am using a 16 GB class 4 micro SD memory card. The camera \\"crashed\\" 2-3 times a day and does not warrant another day of my time.

This camera is more of a liability than a tool. The false security of knowing this camera will show the authorities who was truly to blame in an accident just to find it was frozen when you really needed it...

I returned it for a full refund.

review_body: An excellent dash cam, super high definition video quality, looks great, works great, love it so far!  With a 2.7’’ screen, it is great to see the camera recorded right away, it is very convenient for menu settings, adjustment and video playback, too.  After it’s installed on the windshield and plugged into the cigarette lighter, the camera will record automatically when I turn on the engine. It will automatically turn off when I switch the engine off.  This dash cam shoots really awesome video for both day and night! It records footage up to 1296P Super HD at 30fps, the highest video resolution I can find on Amazon. It can show clearly the license plate and other details in front of my car on the video. While it supports recording 1080P Full HD video at 60fps, technically shoots more images than that at 30fps, particularly fits for high-speed motion, but I cannot find obvious differences on the video.  GPS is very cool and it's showing my route and speed. There’s CD Player comes along with the dash cam, simply put it in my laptop, open the video player and drag a MOV file to it, Google map pops up with route and speed information. GPS also automatically sets the exact date and time to be displayed on videos, simply specify the desired time zone in the menu. Two thumbs up!  As is specified on the detail page, there’re four recording modes in the dash cam, and I tried them all. 1. Loop Recording: I insert a 64GB micro SD card in the dash cam and left it records in the car (with a hard wire kit provides continuous power), and check it the other day. The dash cam records about 8 hours all along, from the time showed on the video, the oldest clips were automatically replaced by new ones. The video clips were cut into average one minute segments on the micro SD card.  2. Emergency Recording: While the dash cam is recording, simply press the “M” key, the current video will be saved immediately and won’t be overwritten by loop mechanism. With a built in Gravity Sensor (G-sensor) the emergency recording mode will trigged automatically when it detects vibration around. This will be vital in an unpredictable incident, the video could be a critical evident in a traffic claim.  3. Motion Detection: A very useful feature, if an object passes in front of the vehicle, Dash Cam automatically starts detection and records motion. Without additional changes to setting, it can automatically detect and record a person approaching the parked car, whether to vandalize or steal from the car. You need to buy an additional hard wiring to provide continuous power.  4. Time Lapse Mode: A wonderful entertainment technique that records a scene or objects that has a slow state-of-change and turns it into a video that plays back in high speed. Have your camera stationary on something that changes slowly (e.g. plants growing) and start recording for hours or even days. Hours and hour’s worth of photos are compressed into a video with merely few minutes playtime, thus creating a time lapsing effect. It’s a pity that only 1sec/5sec/30sec for option in the menu.  On the video, there shows the real time, car plate, and driving speed, all can be set in the menu. Make sure you set the date and time correctly when you install your camera. This will be helpful when you have to offer competent evidence to avoid traffic claims.  While the dash cam is recording, short press the “Down” key, then the audio won’t be recorded; press the “Up” key, the screen will turn off and the cameras still keeps on recording, press the “Power” key, the IR LEDs will be activated. The shortcut keys have very corresponding icons showed clearly on the screen.  Thanks for the new generation mounting, the dash cam could be rotated 90 degree up and down, and when you push it to the topside, you can rotate it around, making it’s available to record inside and outside of your car.  The car charger seems high quality with a Blue LED and an extra USB port which can be used to charge my phone. Very Nice Design!  There’s HDMI cable in the package, but I still have not test it.  Con. 1. Expensive. Though coming with new features and better footage, the price is still a little  high for me. 2. Low capacity battery. I understand most dash cams are designed to work with car power supply, but camera with thus high tech. should have better battery, right? 3. Unspecified User Manual. There’re just basic instructions and operations, no further details.

review_headline: Update: New generation cord sent to me free, works as it should!  Excellent customer service and communication. Would buy again.
review_body:
This is an update, December 1, 2013 for the new cord which I received for free.

As you can see from my previous review below, the first cord I received did not work. I posted a 2 star review and returned the cord to Amazon for a refund. The seller contacted me immediately, explained that the cords had been updated, and that I would receive a new generation one for free, in 7 to 10 working days. I did receive the cord and it works as it should, charging the phone as well as transferring data. I am very impressed with the customer service from this seller, the contact was prompt and they went out of their way to rectify the situation. The cord has a great warranty as well, in case it does fail. When I first plugged it in, it hesitated to make a connection. I used some Deoxit gold on the contacts, and haven't had a problem since. Link to Deoxit on Amazon:

[[ASIN:B003D8EA7A DeoxIT%C2%AE GOLD Liquid squeeze solution]]

This is the original review of the cord which did not work:
When I plugged this into my computer and phone, nothing happened. No charging. I plugged it into an AC powered USB port, still nothing. I wiggled and pushed this way and that at the phone end, and achieved a connection, but the connection was lost when I let go the pressure applied. I applied DeoxIT D100L to attempt to improve the connection, but it did not solve the problem.

The cable appears to be well made, and it would be hard to tell the difference between this and the apple product, except for the fact that it did not work properly. It was shipped promptly, and in the package was an offer for a free cable if I were to review the product. Well, here is that review, and the product would have received 5 stars if it made a reliable connection. It will be going back tomorrow via Amazon Prime, and I've not yet decided whether to try another one of these, or wait for the free one first and see if that one works better. The extra length would be a real advantage, the Iphone 5C battery only lasts about 3/4 of a day with normal use, and being tethered with the 3' factory cord while using the phone is a real pain in the butt. Judging by the distribution of ratings, it seems that a predictable percentage of these cables will not work properly, but the low price, quick shipping, easy Amazon return, and promise of a free cable make this a reasonable risk to take. If/when I receive another one of these, I will review it again on its own merits. If the next one is good, I will buy another one or two for backup and alternate locations.

product_title: Etekcity® Nagoya NA-771 SMA Female 144-440MHz 2.15 dbi 10W Whip Single Antenna for All Two-way Radios (Especially for Baofeng UV-3R UV5R KG-UV6D PX-888K)
review_body:
I bought this from the vendor Etekcity®. Looks like an authentic Nagoya NA-771, based on reviews that suspect bogus ones have stickers rather than a painted logo at the base as shown in the photo. Arrived in an orange plastic ZipLock®-style display sleeve, front side clear, with markings \\"Reuex Industrial Co., Ltd.\\" There's a QR Barcode square, with a logo in red with both the Nagoya and Reuex graphics. There's even a spelling error to further authenticate that this is Made in China. (\\"Flexiable\\" Spring Whip)

Specifications on the package claim 2.15dB gain at 144MHz, and 3.0dB gain at 430MHz. This same antenna body apparently comes terminated in a variety of connectors, according to the hand-marked choices. This, as ordered, is an SMA-F, with others including SMA-M, BNC and Motorola.

Carefully screwed it onto the UV5RA, and immediately felt a rough spot on the threads. Worked it back and forth, it seemed to clear up and now is fine.

Antenna does NOT fully seat into the raised plastic circle on the radio around the antenna connection. The gap is less than 1/16\\" (0.1mm), visible but not as bad as other antennas I've used. For example, I have a monoband VHF antenna, SMA-F, with a gap twice as bad as the Nagoya. I had cut and am using a thin piece of neoprene fuel line as a washer. Placed it under the Nagoya, threaded it down and compressed the washer for a tight fit, and it's good.

Standard reception test is to find the weakest NOAA weather radio station on 162MHz VHF, plant the radio on the desk in one location, and swap antennas to compare. The Nagoya does better than the monoband VHF antenna, and way better than the stock UV5RA antenna.

Not sure yet how much I like the extended length of this antenna. The wangle-dangle had better be worth improved reception and transmit over a shorter version. Physics suggest that's the case, but it's a tradeoff for sure.

Have not yet tested on UHF. Will decode the QR square and see what else they want to tell me.

review_headline: Just one quibble keeps this from 5 stars
review_body:
[[VIDEOID:d4811eb8e3fe67c204c859a6550097d1]] For the price, this is a nice bluetooth speaker. It's a good size - not too big, but big enough for good sound (\\"good sound\\" being relative - I think this has quite good sound for the price, but not as good when compared to $100+ options). It's got a quality feel - nice surface, the right amount of heft, everything is solid, no squeaks, no rattles. It has a good feature set - Bluetooth, speakerphone, line in, *and* line out. And, in my opinion, it's attractive.

However, when paired with one of my phones (Kata i4), there was noise (which, sadly, doesn't come across on the video) when using the phone to move between songs as well as when switching into/out of Bluetooth pairing. I didn't notice that with a different phone (Nexus 6) when pairing, but...the Kata i4 has paired with numerous other Bluetooth devices without issue. So, I suspect this is an issue with the B-trek, and that's why I'm going with 4 stars - when used as a Bluetooth speaker, there were some sound/interference issues, which isn't as good as I'd like.

BUT: If you want to use this as a line-in device, I had zero problems when doing so. When connecting headphones (scenario: you've got nice wired cans, want to listen to a Bluetooth device but don't want to be physically connected to it because it's across the room or people would trip on the cord), I had zero problems... although, to be fair, I didn't test that for long, as it's not a typical use case for me. When I just let it play and didn't change songs, it was fine. It worked as a speakerphone perfectly well for a two minute call to my daughter.

So... it might work great for you. For me, there was just the one problem, but I had to dock a star.

I received a free sample for evaluation purposes. Please feel free to ask questions in the comments and I'll answer as soon as I'm notified.

product_title: Pinnacle- 3 In 1 Car Kit MP3 Player FM Transmitter SD/MMC/USB Card Reader Hands Free + Remote
review_body:
Cons: The instructions are worthless. They do not include any illustrations. They cover very little. They are written in Chinglish. Transferring files to the device is a chore at first, as one (I did, at least) has to download an unsigned USB driver. Windows XP warns against unsigned drivers, but I had to download it to see the device in My Computer. Also, for some reason, it assigned and claimed two separate drives when plugged in. I just ignored the second one (it has zero capacity anyway) and used the first one.

Pros: It works, or has for one month, which I assume would have revealed 90% of potential malfunctions. If you understand what the device is supposed to do, it’s very simple to figure out, and then the worthless instructions become a source of amusement and enjoyment. Once the driver was installed to see the device, downloading .mp3s from the computer is copy-and-paste simple. When I ordered the device, Amazon stated that it would not be delivered for about six weeks: It ships directly from China. As it turned out, the wait was much shorter. I ordered 29 November. Delivery was 13 December. Putting it in the power outlet of the truck and tuning the radio and device to a mutual FM frequency was quick and easy. The frequency I tuned to on the truck radio had some noise from a far-off station. When turned on, the device just over-rode that, and its signal came through loud, clear, and uncluttered. The device follows subdirectory structures, so if you copy a subdirectory to its memory (a particular album, for example), it will play that subdirectory as a whole before moving on to the next subdirectory’s contents. I can’t speak for the quality of sound, really. I’m playing lossy .mp3 files through the two door speakers of a regular-cab pick-up. It is good enough. It has a headphone jack. Four GBs of memory is loads of .mp3 files. Fill it up, and you’ll have days’ worth of audio. Time will tell on the internals, but the device’s body issurprisingly sturdy. It comes with a short USB cable and a spare fuse. The remote is a tiny little thing, but works fine.

Bottom line: For the price and what it does, if it continues to work for six months, I’ll feel I got the bargain of the century. If it croaks after that, I’d happily order another.

review_headline: Better than my old school cassette adapter!
review_body:
This is so much nicer than using the old cassette player corded adapter! I have OLD cars. 1994 Ford Explorer for one. Old school cassette player so I just used one of those adapters that plugs into the headphone jack on your phone/whatever. Problem was, if you didn't fiddle around with the volumes on them, they would sound oh so terrible! AND you were limited by that cord running between your phone and the cassette player.
PROs:
I live in the sticks. I mean remote. If you get 5 miles away from the biggest town, you've got no reception. Even satellite is hindered here because of steep mountainous terrain. So no radio. Pick one of the frequencies on this thing. Any of them. They all work.
No more cords dangling around just waiting to get snagged by the driver... You get the picture.
Plenty of ways to listen to music. If you can't get your phone to Bluetooth, or if you have a device that can't Bluetooth, then load a micro SD with WMA or mP3 songs.
You can charge your phone using the USB port, so you don't lose the use of the lighter "port" for charging.
You can use either your phone or the Jebsen to control music functions. You can skip ahead using the buttons on the adapter, as well as control the volume by turning the knob. Plus, using the Jebsen to skip tracks makes more safety sense since you shouldn't be messing with your phone while driving anyway. If they see you using a phone while driving around here, expect to get a ticket.
Small enough to throw in the glove box, jockey box, or whatever you call them these days.
Once paired, the unit quickly connects to your phone. Like it's sitting there waiting to connect...

CONs:

product_title: Ivation Water Resistant Shockproof Bluetooth 4.0 Speaker - Rated IPX7 for Full Immersion in Water - with Built-in 2200mAh Battery for 6 Hours Playtime
review_headline: It has a solid performance for a Bluetooth and water resistant speaker with good sound!
review_body:
[[VIDEOID:f48e56868d9c3b5131e612824cd779af]]This is a very good waterproof Bluetooth speaker for home, office, travel and use on vacation. It is certified to IPX7 which means that it can be submerged to depths of 1 meter for 30 minutes with no ingress of water. It is also dust and dirt resistant. It can connect to your MP3 player using its Bluetooth 4.0 system and in my testing is had a range of 30 to 35 feet shooting through 2 walls of my home. You can also use your own 3.5 mm plug stereo auxiliary cable to connect a device that does not have a Bluetooth option.

The speaker has a built in Lithium battery that is rated at 2200 mAh at 3.7 VDC and it can play your music for up to 9 hours uninterrupted. It takes about 3 to 4 hours to charge using your computer's USB port, a USB wall charger or a USB car charger.

The sound quality is good out of the speaker with solid bass and clear treble. It uses a dual cone speaker system with a passive subwoofer built into the speaker case.

This speaker has locations on the back to attach a lanyard and it would be a nice speaker to hang in your shower to allow you to listen to your music or radio broadcasted from your phone or tablet. Just make sure that the silicone flap that covers the charging input port and the auxiliary input port is securely pushed down and sealed to maintain the water proof rating of the speaker.

Everything worked well on the speaker except the use of the speaker as a phone remote. When someone called me I could hear them clearly and loudly. On their end of the call my voice was very low and hard to hear. I switched places and it was indeed low, even when they picked up the speaker and spoke directly into the front of it. The speaker has a built in microphone but it was really muted in its volume pickup.

In my video I show how to use the speaker and pair it with Bluetooth. I also made voice control phone calls and that feature worked fine. Overall I liked this speaker a lot. As a speaker to be used as a phone remote it is a 3 star but as a Bluetooth waterproof speaker it is a 5 star. I rated it overall as a 5 star item because of its capability to be used around water.

review_body:
Update: After writing the review below, I received a message from the seller which is shown as a comment to this post. Based on the content of that message, I'm changing my rating to four stars. If the cover is as strong as they claim, the case should do well over time. It's just quite different from the Bear Motion iPad cases, but I agree that having a light-weight case can be a beneficial feature. I appreciate Ebiz explaining the composition of the front cover.

Personally, if I had known, I'd rather pay a few dollars more for a case that seems more substantial. I'm not rough on things so hopefully this case will last for a while. But I'm doubtful that it'll hold up if you're not careful with it. One other thing that might be a small issue for some people -- it doesn't open as easily as my other cases because the front cover is so thin. I'm sure that makes it lighter, but it helps to have a fingernail to get between the front and back covers. I just wish this were more like the other Bear Motion cases that I have.

The only reason this is getting a two instead of a one is because you can use it as a midi interface.

Headphone jack
Loop buttons on the controller for the desired beat lengths.
The ability to recalibrate knobs.
Better scratching and non-reverting BPM changes.

review_headline: Impressive video quality (HD H.264 format) for the price!
review_body:
I was really surprised and impressed when I reviewed my first round of recordings. The HD quality for this price is exceptional. Overall, this is a great solution for those who want a video system in your car on a budget. If you were able to turn off the microphone and screen, battery life would be greatly improved, so I hope a future Firmware update may offer this solution. I also wish that you could connect an external microphone to this camera so you could record outdoor sounds instead of the interior. At the end of the day I am really pleased with my purchase.

Pros:

1.) Massive storage capacity (up to 32GB) on SDHC
2.) Connects to your computer via included USB for charging and file transfer
3.) Cigarette lighter power cord for long trips
4.) Excellent H.264 High Definition video quality
5.) Two-way adjustable mount. You can pivot up and down and swivel left-to-right with two secure tension knobs
6.) Date and time stamp on corner of video
7.) Wide angle lense shoots true panoramic view. Even with my camera mounted on the upper-right side of the windshield I am able to capture the entire front of my vehicle. ***See uploaded photos of my mounted camera***

Cons:

1.) Limited features and basic settings but for the price and purpose this is not a problem for most
2.) Battery life is rougly 3 hours
3.) Inability to disable the LCD screen or microphone to extend battery life
4.) Night recording is poor even with my xenon high intensity headlights and regardless of streetlamps being overhead. The video quality comes out grainy and is no longer high definition as a result of the processing software within the camera itself.

4 out of 5 stars.

Of course to lock it you have to press the 2 buttons on the right, which most of the time fail then it counts it as a new lap.  The 'lap' issue is minor ; w/o locking the watch (which prevent the \\"bezel\\" to be touch  : rain, sweat, trees ,etc...), the watch can stop by itself.  Over the last 3 months, running more or less every day, I may have lost ~ runs like this.  I found also the battery less effective compared with the 305  basically I have to charge it every day).  For some other reason, it sometimes switch display while running ; from the display with time/pace/miles, it goes to the display where you see your virtual partner.  So I still put 1 star because the GPS function is much better (you don't have to wait ~1mn to locate the GPS as with the 305 for example) and I'm sure they are a lot of other useful functions (I mentioned the virtual partner that allow you to see the difference between a previous run) but the whole issue with the touch technology is the bottleneck. product_title: The OontZ Ultra-Portable Wireless Bluetooth Speaker by Cambridge SoundWorks
review_body:

In one store I listened to the Jawbone, it is nice, however I do not think it is any better than this. The Bose is way ahead though, however you can get four of these and have some change.

Some say it drops the signal, well it will. The receiver for BT is typically only good for around 30ft with a direct line of sight. Mine works well in the yard, however if my phone is in my pocket and I turn, sometimes it will drop off, however it does reconnect immediately.

Comparing this little unit to a Bose is ridiculous. You cannot compare a $300 unit to this. My neighbor has the new Bose and it is amazing in my opinion, the bass is very rich and clear. I travel a lot and could see the Bose taking a beating, and I would rather abuse the Oontz and take a chance on breaking it instead.

The speaker will dance around if the surface is very smooth, however if you sit it on its little cloth bag, it won't budge.

This little unit paired up very quickly to my Motorola Photon and you have to power it up by activating the phone's bluetooth first, then powering up the speaker. The Chinese written instructions did not cover this too well.

I've been using mine for a month now, and I have to say I love it. Yes the blue LED is very bright, some complain about this, however we've just completed a road trip and it comes in handy when putting two small kids to bed in a hotel room, it is a useful night light.

If you want absolute sound quality, get the Bose, if you want something that can be tossed into a suitcase, I would only consider the Oontz.

Update, September 7th 2013

I have had this for almost a year now, it has been everywhere and not looked after as well as it could. The charge lasts forever and it sounds better with my new phone. Some of the other bluetooth speakers look prettier, however they cannot match the longevity of the battery of this.

The IMP70D performed beautifully and allowed us to also charge my wife's iPadat the same time.  The value derived from this trip alone was enough to pay for this battery pack. product_title: Alpine EX-10 Advanced iPod Controller with Bluetooth
review_body: I had an in-dash radio with Bluetooth in my old car. I traded it for a pickup that had a factory XM radio in the dash. My old stereo had Sirius. Not wanting to clutter the roof with stick-on antennae, but needing Bluetooth, as I am hearing-impaired decided to get the Alpine eX-10. I made a small shelf for it to sit on, along with the remote, hooked it up and tried it out.    Since my stereo has an Aux Input, I wired it directly to the car stereo. I found that the phonebook will not download, a fact that circumvents the hands-free functions of the phone. When I want to make a call, I have to do so manually, using the phone. I make sure I do this when I am not in traffic, and I have memorized the button pushes to make calls to the two places I call most. The phone sounds great and I can have the conversation without holding the phone to my ear. Sometimes when the person on the other end of the conversation hangs up, the eX-10 realizes this and hangs up for me. If I am expecting a call, I have to use the radio in Aux/CD mode. Since CDs are so 90s, I don't use them. If I forget my iPod, I have to listen to road noise until my call is complete. I will probably get a cell phone with mp3 capabilities and will hopefully get rid of this problem.    I mentioned the iPod. It plays through the eX-10 really well. I do with there were buttons on the front of the unit, so that I didn't have to retrieve the remote any time I want to play another song, answer the phone, etc. A short piece of velcro taped to that aluminum shelf I built keeps the remote within reach and at the same place, so I can pick it up without taking my eyes off the road.    All in all, this is a good unit. I was really pampered with the \\"everyone's everything\\" unit I had before. I am acclimating to the apparent shortcomings of this unit. I can't find another that does Bluetooth and iPod. I'd buy it again.

product_title: Generic Car Dashboard Video Camera Vehicle Video Accident Recorder (2.0" 1080P)
review_body:
Better resolution and performance than some of the slightly cheaper ($25) models. Menus are actually in English. The lens rotation mechanism is loose in any orientation. Will generally stay put, but will vibrate over bumps. I am returning it because the vendor (cool World Plaza) sent me an obviously USED one that was dirty and covered in fingerprints, and missing the mounting plate, making it impossible to mount. I have one other cam to try, if it doesn't work out I may roll the dice and buy another one of these and hopefully end up with a brand-new one that actually includes a mount.

Update 2013-03-31: I sent the first one of these back, and tried a few other cameras, which turned out to be counterfeit junk (you can see my other reviews). So, I took a chance and ordered another one of these, and sent a message to the vendor (David Wu) to make sure to send me a NEW, NON-COUNTERFEIT camera.

That request seems to have paid off. The camera I received is actually pretty great, especially considering it's still in the $50 range. I'm bumping the review up to four stars.

The 720 resolution is actually 720, even though the claimed 1080 modes are fake. Still, 720 is pretty good, it is pretty easy to read license plates of cars in front of me. The menus are in English and easy to understand and navigate. The lens rotation is tight, and both LEDs work (for what that's worth). I'm using a class 4 SanDisk 16GB MicroSD, and it works great, and the files overwrite as intended.

One really cool feature is that all you have to do is use the USB cable/cigarette lighter adapter, and the camera will come on and start recording when the power comes on, and stop recording and turn off when it's removed. My outlets are always hot, so I will be re-wiring to have it activated by the ignition. I will be replacing the 12v-to-5v regulator/cigarette adaptor that came with it, because as others have noted, it DOES interfere with radios, even FM (slightly), and I found that it also greatly reduced the range of my keyless entry. Can't have that. Since it will only be on with the ignition, I'll replace it with a nice simple and RFI-free linear regulator.

At this point, I would definitely buy another one of these cameras, over all of the other 4 or 5 I tried, even though it is twice the price of those others. Totally worth it to avoid the time, hassle, and letdown. Of course, I don't have a high confidence that if I placed another order I would get the same camera. That's something I wish Amazon and their vendor(s) could get worked out. I recommend trying to get it from David Wu, and sending a message through Amazon insisting on a NEW camera. There is no Mfg or model number shown on the packaging, but there is a barcode label that says B0067XVNTG.

We then traveled to the Oregon Coast, arriving on a dry day however the next two days were heavy rain, fog and wind. When we went to leave we found the left camera was fogged up inside the lens and the dry trip home never de-fogged the lens.

When I contacted ASA electronics customer service they treated me like a second or third class citizen. The main issue was due to the fact I had purchased it through Amazon and second that I had installed it myself. I have a degree in electronics and have been remodeling my motorhome for the last year so I know it better than any technician would from Camping World or any other technician.

ASA electronics required proof of purchase which I understood however I was told not to call back and check on the status at a later time and that I would be contacted when they were ready. I am 60 and have dealt with a lot of customer support over the years however ASA electronics is among the worst I have ever seen. I will never buy another ASA electronics product again, which makes Jensen and Voyager and I am sure a lot more. In this economy most customer service has improved...not so with ASA electronics (in my opinion).

product_title: Icom IC-2200H 64Wts. VHF Mobile Transceiver
review_headline: Great Replacement for an Icom IC-2100H
review_body:
Like all of the Icom products made in the last 8-10 years, this one has been a replacement for a flawed unit. The IC-2200H replaces the IC-2100H. The 2100 had a transistor that got too hot and would not allow power setting changes to be made. Icom blamed the customer for using the wrong antenna or damaging the equipment even when they did nothing to it. The 2200 fixed the problem and added some features. The \\"H\\" was a change due to a problem with the handset, which was fixed or replaced.

I give this radio only 4 stars due to this. 2100's and 2200's are great radios and pack a lot of useful features, and at a low price. But be cautious, Icom hires engineers that have no clue and tend to need some work out of the box to be reliable. The common thread from Icom, it is your fault, either pay us for the repair (of our engineering problem), or buy this newer model.

The VHF Marine radios, IC-M602 had little or no RF shielding and the response was to \\"buy an IC-M604). The PCR-1000 could be modded to hear cell phones (analog), and the response was, \\"buy a PCR-1500\\". Predator drones with PCR-1000's had other issues, and the response was \\"buy a PCR-2500\\". My response, \\"why should I buy another Icom\\"?

As for the IC-2200H, this is a great radio and will work well, but be sure to test all features and do a burn in test right after purchase. It is a great entry level radio, or dedicated digital DarkStar radio. Or better yet, buy something that says: \\"Motorola\\", \\"Vertex/Yaesu/Standard\\", or \\"Kenwood\\" on it.

Of course, I live in a mobile home. Aluminum siding, no attic. There is, quite literally, no attic to place this in, and the house's siding seriously reduces all transmission. The solution?

Mount a piece of PVC to the side of the house or in the ground. Where I am, it's windy, so it also has to be encased in a plexiglass box to both protect from rain and falling debris from wind. I'm an enthusiast about flashlights. I have been checking out stores and actually purchased several different types of battery powered lanterns. There are several things that I look for when considering a flashlight and lanterns. 1) Only those that use AA or AAA batteries are considered. Those two batteries are the cheapest and most readily available batteries. Plus, in an emergency, I do not want to be scrambling for different types of batteries (C, D, 9V, CR123, or any other type of specialized battery). 2) The design has to be shock resistant and waterproof. 3) The longest battery life in proportion to the output. I would like an efficient flashlight. 4) Best combination of durability in ratio to size and weight. I look for the lightest and most compact lights that are durable, which is especially important in headlamps and lanterns. This is a review of the Fenix Flashlight White Diffuser Wand that I use with my Fenix LD20 CREE XR-E Flashlight.

I rated the Fenix LD20 a 5.0 out of 5.0 in a previous review due to being extremely bright, having various brightness settings, a neutral white color temperature, a smooth and even beam, considerable throw, being one of the most efficient flashlights, having a rugged build, all of this in a extremely small design, and using AA batteries. I have also purchased the Fenix Headband for 18-22mm Flashlights, which pairs with the Fenix LD20 perfectly. I have also rated this accessory a 5.0 out of 5.0 as it was the most comfortable headband that I have tried, it is fully adjustable, the design is well thought out and durable, and it allows me to use the Fenix LD20 as a headlamp. Being able to use the Fenix LD20 with the diffuser as a lantern is one thing, but being able to use it hands free as a headlamp is very convenient.

I am extremely pleased with my purchase of the Fenix Flashlight White Diffuser Wand. 1) It allows me to turn the Fenix LD20 into a lantern that is bright, neutral white, that is more efficient than all of the other lanterns that I own, lightweight, compact, durable, and uses only 2 AA batteries. 2) The diffuser appears to be constructed well and is very rugged. It has handled drops very well. 3) It does diffuse light very evenly and it has exceeded my expectations. I was expecting lines and uneven spots, but did not observe any of those things. 4) The fit on the Fenix LD20 is snug and secure. This also exceeded my expectations as did not expect the diffuser to fit so well. 5) The Fenix LD20 with the diffuser makes such an impressive lantern, brighter than any of the electric lanterns out there. On Turbo, the Fenix LD20 with the diffuser will light up rooms. 6) The Fenix LD20 has multiple brightness settings, which makes it more versatile than any of the lanterns out there, which usually only have an off/on or high/low setting. Having a low setting that lasts 70 hours on 2 AA batteries is such an advantage.

One picky thing that may be brought to attention is that the Fenix LD20 does heat up when in use, more so when set on Turbo. The Fenix Diffuser does cover the head of the flashlight snugly, which means that heat will be trapped in the head. I have not experienced problems with this, but it is possible that this may cause overheating problems that have been noted by another reviewer.

Conclusion: Overall, the Fenix Flashlight White Diffuser Wand is another top quality accessory that matches extremely well with the Fenix LD20. Fenix continues to impress and I am very thankful for finding such well-thought, high quality products. product_title: XLink Cellular Bluetooth Gateway
review_body: We recently decided to drop our landline and go all cellular.  I purchased one of these XLink units and a new cell phone from Verizon to go with it (it's a Samsung Convoy and supports all of the latest bluetooth profiles).  This phone is dedicated to the unit, meaning that the cell phone sits next to the XLink and never moves.  The XLink then connects to our 5.8Ghz base station, which services six wireless extensions.  The phone, the base station, and XLink are all on top of the same table.     Pairing up the cell phone to the XLink could not be easier.  It was also easy to connect the XLink to my computer to download the latest software update.  Then things went downhill.  As we used the system over a period of a week or so, we ran into two major problems.    1. The sound quality was considerably worse than our landline. There was no static, so I don't believe it was an interference issue.  Rather, the sound was very much like a speaker phone. When a person was not talking, the line sounded dead, but when they spoke, the first word of their sentences would be clipped. Conversations were not duplex--two people could not talk at the same time or overlap in their speech. Again, just like a speakerphone.  The overall sound quality was a bit distorted too--like the gain on an amplifier being turned up too high.  Anyway, I contacted XLink support about this and they said that this is basically typical of a bluetooth connection and there is nothing that could be done about it.  Strike one.    2. In addition to this problem, I had repeated connection problems.  This happened three times before I finally decided enough was enough. After two days of being connected, like clockwork, the phone would get into a kind of weird funk.  The blue light indicating a valid bluetooth connection remained lit, and you could both receive and place calls, but you could neither hear nor speak to the other caller.  It was like the phone was fully muted.  The only way to fix the problem was tounplug the XLink and re-pair.  XLink support suggested that I download the latest software, but I had already done that.  After three instances of this along with the first problem, I was starting to wonder if I had made a mistake in disconnecting the land line.  Strike two.    Being rather frustrated, I re-read some of the reviews here, and based on a hint from one of the reviewers, I went down to BestBuy and picked up a vtech DS6321-3 system just to try someone else's technology (Amazon also sells this).  This unit has a bluetooth compatible base station and three extension phones for just $89--only $10 more than the XLink.   I brought it home and was immediately amazed at the sound quality.  It was night and day over the XLink. Almost indistinguishable from the landline--and full duplex too.  No clipping or distortion.  I have not had any weird connection issues with it either.  It just works.  You also get full bluetooth integration with the vtech, such as the ability to download your phonebook to the handsets and notification of voicemail. I will need to buy a few extra handsets at $18 a pop to fully replace my old system, but the difference in quality is well worth it.  Strike three.  The XLink is on its way back.

product_title: ALURATEK LIBRE 7IN COLOR MULTI-MEDIA - EBOOK READER WITH 2GB BUILT-IN MEM - AEBK07FS
review_headline: The Answer to All the Problems I Had with Kindle!
review_body:
I've had a Kindle for about six months, but reading on it was getting tiresome, mostly because of the screen flashing to black between each page, the glare on the screen, and the ugliness of the device and the text. I found the black frame around the e-ink screen distracting, and the large progress at the bottom was bugging me too (I put a rubber band around it, but then kept getting distracted by the rubber band).

So I picked up this ereader off the Aluratek website for $50 (refurbished). It came with the firmware update already installed, and 100 books. The 100 books actually weren't bad, I kept quite a few... (to delete the books, go to My Computer and then look for your E: drive, click on it and you'll see the books to delete). One thing about the AC is that you can't put the books in a directory, so I'd recommend only uploading a few books that you want to read immediately and then upload the rest as you'd like to read them.

Here are some things I liked about the Aluratek Color:
*Glowing screen for reading in the dark. Would be great on a car trip (although the battery only lasts about 8 hours, but if you charge it right before it should be fine). The brightness is adjustable within a wide range. If you're like me and your house has ****tty lighting, then you'll love this feature because you can go from room to room without having to find a light enough spot to read. No noticeable glare on screen.
*Weight - I actually like the fact that it's heavier than the Kindle - it's the perfect size to hold on to and makes you feel like you're holding a book in your hands.
*Style - Damn, this thing is pretty. The white looks very futuristic, the screen is tall and graceful, there is no keyboard mucking up the front, and the FULL TITLES of the books are displayed! Great if you read a lot of Fantasy and you want to see what number a book is in a series and the name. The large white columns on either side give it an oddly classical look,and the continuous white doesn't distract the eye.
*Easy to upload to with Calibre.
*SD slot can expand the memory (not that you'll need much for books).
Automatic rotate depending on whether you're holding it portrait or landscape. Landscape is nice because it makes for very long lines.
*Fonts on the pages look really nice.
*PROGRESS METER IS VERY LIGHT!!! THANK YOU! You have to bring it close to see it, so it's not distracting at all.
*Menu and welcome screen are both very pretty and inviting. Allure-atek indeed. haha

Cons:
*Doesn't do pdfs well. Can do them, but making the text larger is very slow to the point where reading is impossible.
*No annotation - although annotating on the Kindle was a pain in the ass, so I don't really miss it.
*Low-ish battery life. (8hrs).

Conclusion:
The Aluratek Color did everything I expected (and was much prettier than I expected!). I don't think I'll be using my Kindle again anytime soon, the LCD screen is much easier to read off and the chassis seems solid enough I don't have to keep it in a case all the time. Love it!

product_title: Sony Walkman Portable All-in-one Skip-Free CD Player - Digital AM / FM Radio Tuner, Clip Style Earbud Headphones, 40 preset FM stations, Digital Mega Bass Sound, AVLS & CD-R/RW Playback, D-FJ041 White
review_body:
Delivered within 2 days. I've used it about 5 times, so far, usually while riding a bicycle, and it works as advertised. Appears to be well made and solid. Has good range and adjustment subtlety on volume. Buttons are small and poorly marked; over time I expect to get accustomed to that. I like the earphones very much - they stay in place even while moving around.

Update, 4 months later:

It's still going strong and I like it a lot. I mostly use it while riding my bicycle. Sound quality and reliability are good. It restarts on the CD at the position when I last turned it off, even if I take the CD out and then put it back in!

The main drawback is its size - it's definitely big and bulky, not like an MP3 player. But I have a carry-belt that it fits into, so I can make that work. To me the size tradeoff is worthwhile because I listen to \\"The Great Courses\\" so I can go through a lot of CD's in a short time, and it's easier managing the CD's directly, rather than ripping each CD and then transferring the files into a phone/MP3 player.

The buttons aren't great - small and hard to read what each one does. When riding my bike in intermittent traffic I'm always wanting to increase and decrease the volume as necessary and it's a pain to take the thing out and tweak the volume while riding my bike. So, I have started on putting the volume pretty high and then taking the ear buds out of my ears but letting them hang right next to the ears; this effectively lowers the volume going in my ears. When the ambient traffic noise gets loud again, I just push the ear buds back into my ears. This is much easier than pressing the volume buttons.

By the way, I really like having the radio (FM and AM!) and CD player all in one. You can program presets in the radio.

I've used it around 2 hours per week and had to change the batteries after about 3-4 months (qty 2 AA batteries). One tricky thing is that I thinkit's possible to leave the radio on when you put it down and you wouldn't know it, so you could drain the battery in just a few days.

The sound is about what you'd expect on a small, inexpensive stereo, but it's fine for the office. I was not thrilled to see the custom connectors for the speakers, though. It means I'll have to do some soldering to add more wire if I ever need to put the speakers very far from the head unit.

The FM reception with the included wire antenna isn't bad, considering the stereo is inside a metal-framed building.

I haven't tried the iPod port (I switched to Samsung last year), so can't say how/if it works.

The USB port works fine. It takes a little while to read the stick, but that seems to be common with all the USB-equipped devices I've used, including my JVC car stereo. This stereo can't read as many files/folders as my JVC unit does, but that's not a big issue.

CD play works as expected; no problems thus far.

This isn't high fidelity, but it also doesn't cost as much as a mid- or high-end receiver. Use it in the right surroundings, don't plan on setting the speakers too far away, and manage your expectations, and you'll be quite happy with it.

product_title: Slash 4X4 VXL RTR with TQi 2.4GHz and 7-Cell Battery and Charger
review_body: I cannot find any negatives about this truck at all. Charge up the battery and you are ready to go. It is that simple. And it is quite fast for a single battery truck. I also have a Traxxas gas truck, an HPI gas truck, a CEN gas truck and a Traxxas E-Maxx. Two things I really like about this truck is that first it is waterproof and it is also Brushless. You can upgrade it to an 11.1v Lipo battery and then it will fly (well almost).     It comes with 1 Traxxas 8.4v NiMh 3000 mah battery pack, much better than what everyone else supplies with their RTR Electric Cars/Trucks. And I was able to buy 2 more battery packs for under $50!. My nephew bought one at the same time and we raced at a nearby R/C dirt track with huge double and triple jumps and tight banked turns. We went through 6 batteries running for more than a couple hours (with breaks). The Slash was a lot of fun, with great acceleration and handling. We ran them straight out of the box, no adjustments, no break-in, no assembly, just put in a battery and go! After all than running the only problem was some wear to the paint on the body above the tires. Probably caused by all the jumps, so if you are going to run on a similar track then you might want to tighten the suspension a little. But other than that there were no other problems and we hit each other a few times and flipped over quite a few times. A very rugged truck.     If you are getting tired of Gas RC Cars/Trucks, then the Slash 4x4 is for you. If you are just getting into RC Trucks and want an outstanding starter truck then the Slash 4x4 is for you. A lot of fun and very reliable with parts available everywhere.    Keep in mind though that on Traxxas products, there is essentially No Warranty. While Traxxas claims the electronics are warranteed for life, it will cost you to exchange the electronics. The power button stuck on the ESC and it cost me $55 to get it exchanged and the truck was only about 3 months old! If you have no problems then the Slash is the best stadium type truck but HPI Racing has a real warranty.

product_title: Sony PRS-600BC Touch Edition E-Book Reader
review_headline: Very functional, user friendly, I really like the touchscreen feature
review_body: I'm a first time buyer of e-readers.  I hope my comments are helpful for other potential buyers.    Why Sony PRS-600?    1. Support of the PDF and EPUB open and international standards.  Being in an IT oriented career, I have had enough headaches with proprietary formats to know to avoid them as much as possible.    2. I can buy books from multiple e-book stores.  Suppliers with proprietary formats limit your choice of retailers (usually just to one). I believe the issue of available titles will balance itself out in the near future as the e-book market expands.     3. I must clarify that the wireless download, though nice, was not a big issue for me. I usually research and plan my reading material in my computer and with the internet. Also, for the moment I `m not interested in the magazine and periodical subscription services.    What I like:  1. The touch screen:  It really facilitates and enhances your reading.  Lookup of words in the dictionary, references to footnotes, highlighting and writing notes are quite easy with the touch screen. (** Note: Yes, there is a glare, but I have always been able to effortlessly find an angle where this is non-issue.)    2. The dictionary: English is not my first language and I have found out this tool to be very useful, particularly with the classics which usually have non-frequently used or outdated words.    3. The free book libraries:  Yes, there are multiple sites with free books. I'm amazed at the quantity of free e-books available.  Most of them in PDF and EPUB format. No problem so far downloading and reading these e-books in the PRS-600.    4. The font sizes:  My eyes are not young. I really appreciate being able to increase the font size as needed.    What I don't like:  1. Sony PC software is not user friendly.  I'm using Calibre as a primary library management tool, and it's pretty cool. With Calibre this has become a non-issue.    What I would like to see:  2. Full support (books and dictionary) for e-books in Spanish.   3. A lot of competition so that the devices get better, cheaper and the number of titles expands dramatically.    Some additional comments:  1. The screen glare:  Again, I must stress that this is really a non-issue for me.  My suggestion to potential buyers is to compare and balance the flexibility you get with the touch screen vs. the glare and clarity.  After using the device I think it is a nice tradeoff.    In summary, I'm very satisfied with this device and look forward to the future developments in the e-reader market.  My final suggestion to potential buyers is to go and test the devices and buy what fits your needs and preferences.

product_title: Eco-nique natural Hemp Brown case cover for Barnes & Noble Nook - Book Style
review_body: I got this cover cause 1) Looked cool, 2) Looked Functional.  The price ($37.99 abouts) is about the same as most other nook covers out there but the others didn't look nearly as good (especially for guys) and look bare bone functional.  I've had this cover for a few days hard reading and have been impressed. That said, let's get down to the nitty gritty.      QUALITY/DURABILITY:     Stitching: Very well done. I looked the whole thing over for loose threads and sloppy thread termination (you know where they stop stitching and cut off the excesss) and haven't found any of that. Someone did a good job.       Leather: It's a Poly Leather that from inspection seems to be well made. Doesn't feel or look like the nasty cheap stuff. Time will tell.      Hemp:  My first hemp product. Like a mix between Burlap, Canvas, and Tweed lol. Course abration like cement wouldn't be good for it but I wouldn't bat an eye about sliding this across wood table tops or floors on a daily basis. With that in mind, I think it's sturdy.      Metal snap:  Seems both peices are well secured on both sides.    FIT:     Device install/removal:  Easy, yet snug. Excellent fit. Someone did their maf homwerx.      Security(If I shake it, will it fall out):  You could play catch with it and it wouldn't budge. I've found myself mindlessly twirling it around (like I do to my other books) when I'm not paying attention. On top of the snug fit, it's got a half inch leather tab that velcros the top in. Good feature, executed well.    COMFORTABLE:    Feel in hand:  Surprisingly comfortable. I didn't like how the nook, by itself is so thin, but with the cover on it I find it to be just right.  One interesting aspect I wasn't expecting was the front and back cover are cushioned. There's a board on the inside to give the cover rigidity like a baseball cap but then it's got padding on top of that. Besides the added protection it strangely makes it pleasurable and comfortable to touch.      Feel of Hemp:  A soft fibrous texture like a tightly woven tweed (just got a girls opinion). The padded front and back make it even softer. Straight up though, it's just comfortable. I'd rather hold this on a hot day then something leather.      Feel of Folded Cover Read:  The coolest thing about this cover so far, besides the design on the cover, is that you can fold the front cover back and use the snap closure to keep it there.     PROTECTION:    Corner Drops: This is the only bummer I've found so far. If you were to drop this on it's upper right or lower right corner, with your nook inside, your nooks gonna feel the pain. The cover doesn't extend out much at all past the nooks corners. The top left and bottom left corners of the nook will feel a little pain but are afforded decent protection from the binding of the cover.  After thinking the problem through though I decided it'd it's not bad at all for something that fits my nook rather then engulf and bulk-ify it.      Flat Drops: Well and good. I don't see my nook getting hurt from a front or back hit.    EASE OF USE:     Headjack/USB/Speakers access: Good. All accessible With the cover closed.      Attachable Light: I'm using one and it fit just fine.    OVER ALL:    All in all, this cover is rock'n awesome. I feel that for the money spent on it I get the protection/coolness/usability that I wanted with a flare of unique.  I'm even more happy that I didn't spend the same amount for the ones I saw displayed at Barnes & Nobles that were hardly bare bone functional at the same or higher price.  On a side note, I feel like by purchasing this I helped fund an eco-terrorist group.     I do own this and use it everyday, if you have any questions about it that I didn't cover, comment, if Amazon will alert me on your post then I'll answer. Rock on!

product_title: Sony PRS-600BC Touch Edition E-Book Reader
review_headline: Brief review of Sony Touch Reader I(The Kindle's Slight Inferior)
review_body: I am a kindle owner and have been looking into the Sony Touch. My verdict is that the Sony is slightly inferior to the kindle. Though an interesting machine, its benefits are not as beneficial as one might think at first blush.     Quite simply, the Sony Touch can do just about everything that the Amazon kindle can do. One can highlight and annotate (with a stylus rather than a cursor). One can easily turn pages (with a thumb-flick rather than a button-press) and jump to sections of the book easily. And the Sony even has features the kindle does not have: one can draw on a blank 'page,' read .pdf files natively, zoom in on text by degrees, and download public domain google books...er...wait.     Here is where I interject by saying that many of these features really aren't as good as they first appear. Many people, for instance, are sold on the idea of being able to download any public domain google book. Allegedly, the kindle cannot do this...except for...it can! With help from some very free and easy-to-use software online (calibre), one can convert any downloaded google book into a file format that amazon recognizes. The conversion is easy, flawless, and gives the kindle user access to every google book that Sony owners can get.     Second, many people are sold on the touch screen. Imagine highlighting, annotating, and turning the page without having to use cumbersome buttons and cursors. But this sounds better than it is! The thumb-flick page-turning method, for instance, basically means that one must read with two hands (rather than reading with one on a kindle, where the page turn button is located where one's thumb can click it). And if you swipe your thumb too hard on the Sony screen, it thinks you want to highlight; too light, and it won't work. As for operating annotations with a stylus, this is no easier, harder, quicker, or slower than the kindle's cursor method.     The biggest drawback to the Sony Touch is the clumsy software and lack of selection. Every book available for the Sony (that I've checked) is available for the kindle at the same or lesser price. But by no means is the opposite true: every book available for the kindle is by no means available for the Sony. Long and short: the kindle simply has a better and more cost-effective selection of books. And in the week that I tried out my Sony Touch, the software malfunctioned three times.     I give the Sony Touch 3 stars because in many ways, it is the Kindle's equal. The screen is great, it is easy to use, its features are good, and its battery life is PHENOMENAL (one area where the Sony has the Kindle beat by far)! But the features that make the Sony seems like the favorite are, on closer examination, really not all that great. The kindle can, via conversion, access any public domain google book and the touchscreen is just as much trouble as it is an asset. And I have not noticed that the Sony handles .pdf files natively any better than the kindle does via conversion.     So, it is close to a toss-up but...it is the Kindle by a nose!

I also connected it to my flat panel TV, which is on the wall above the radio, and use the Ambiance 2 radio as a sound bar.
The voices sound clearer, and the bass is better, than my $400 Yamaha sound bar (and that's all it does) that is connected to my main TV.

I own a high end audio system, and know what great sounding music is like. I have to say that the fidelity and dynamics of the music that comes out of this little radio is mind blowing.
Especially when you consider how little this radio costs.

I haven't used the alarm clock function, but it looks like it is easy to set (two separate alarm times can be set).

This product would make a great gift. Give one to yourself.

product_title: Forerunner 110 by Garmin
review_headline: The Forerunner 110 does not perform as advertised
review_body: I purchased the Forerunner 110 with the intention of obtaining consistently accurate (or near accurate) readings of the mileage I completed while working out in the city, on a quarter of a mile track as well as in the mountains where I hike. I know my workout pace and the precise distances of the paths I workout on. Although Garmin's website advertises this model to provide accurate readings of mileage completed near tall buildings and under the cover of trees, based on my experiences and a friends, it doesn't, and the readings are off at times up to twenty percent! In fact,I have contacted Garmin regarding this problem on several occasions and although they had me download an updated program for this GPS watch it did not help whatsoever. I even exchanged this model due to the possibility that it was damaged and obtained a new one, but the same issue was immediately apparent; it failed to calibrate accurate mileage completed by a significant amount, at least twenty percent on the measured quarter of a mile track,in the city near tall buildings as well as on mountain hikes under the cover of trees. I returned this second watch and got my money back.    It should also be noted that when encountering any problems with Garmin watches the wait time to speak with a technician is inordinate,at times up to thirty minutes, which is grossly unacceptable.     Based on my experience as well as that of a friend,I would not recommend this product because it does not provide the level of accuracy it is advertised to provide.

product_title: BlueAnt S4 Bluetooth Car Speakerphone Kit [USEN-BAW-S4]
review_headline: Worst bluetooth device EVER! Don't buy if you're looking for hands free in the car.
review_body: This is the worst bluetooth device I've ever tried to work with. Pairing the device is easy enough, and it looks great; the design itself is actually quite slick. The functionality of this \\"true handsfree\\" device is anything but.     You say \\"Blueant, speak to me\\" and that turns it on, ready for a voice prompt. You'd think at that point you could add someone's name and their phone number to the memory of this device (I don't think it actually has any memory at all) so that you can then say \\"call Chuck\\" or even \\"dial 650-255-5939\\". Nope. Not even close. You can do nothing even close to that.      What it does allow you to do is use your phone's voice recognition functionality to make voice activated calls. So basically, this just allows you to use your phone's speakerphone function over the bluetooth function. Useless. Why on earth would you buy a second device in order to use your phone's speakerphone? It doesn't make any sense.     If you only need to receive calls in your car and never need to dial anyone else, or you only want your text messages read out loud to you when they arrive, then this device might be ok for you. But please make sure that you never need to dial someone else, because this device will be totally useless to you.     For something that was almost $100, claims to be specifically designed for use in the car, and claims to be true handfree and voice controlled, I can not even begin to describe how disappointed I am.     After 4 days of trying to use this with an iPhone 3GS and an Android Nexsus S I'll be returning it and choosing another option.     TL;DR - don't waste your money, this thing is a piece of junk that doesn't function as described.

product_title: GOgroove SMARTmini BT ADVANCED Wireless In-Car Bluetooth FM Transmitter with Charging, Music Control and Hands-Free Calling for ANDROID, iPhone, Blackberry and Windows Smartphones
review_body:
I would recommend this item to others, but it isn't without faults.

First, I can't imagine buying the full size version of this. I find this thing bigger than it needs to be. I can't comment on the charging ability as I only use it for the FM transmitter and Bluetooth abilities in my company vehicle ('06 F150). I also haven't used any of the call features (and don't plan to) so again that's not reviewed here.

Con's:
- Doesn't fit tight enough in the 12V socket. I have had it come loose and lose power a couple of different times.

- It's feature to find an FM frequency is about as bad as it can get. Instead of picking a frequency that is clear it instead picks a frequency that is on a radio station with the strongest transmitter of any station in Central Ohio (WNCI). Needless to say that doesn't work out well. Luckily, you can manually tune to whatever frequency you want

- No power button

- Only auto-pairs to my iPhone 5 about 25% of the time. Luckily, a quick push on the blinking phone button quickly pairs it. I almost put this in the Pro category, but it is a negative since it doesn't consistently do it one way or the other.

Pro's:
- Once a good frequency is picked, the sound quality is pretty decent.

- Good Bluetooth range

- Decent volume. Not as loud as my Sirius unit hardwired via an FM Direct connection, but close enough.

For my uses (streaming music/Sirius online) in my company vehicle on the crappy OEM head unit, it does its job well enough. For many people, I would suggest upgrading to something with a hardwired connection; either a PAC adapter for your OEM head unit or an aftermarket head unit. An FM transmitter will always give up sound quality - I knew this going in, and purchased this ONLY because my portable Sirius unit died again (not a shocker) and didn't want to be without my Howard while I waited on a replacement.

I most often tuck the IMP70D in the Scottevest that I wear to conveniently carry my iPad and iPhone in. The flat battery fits comfortably in an interior pocket just below where the iPhone pocket is, the two connected by the iPhone's USB cord. I am no longer concerned about a dead iPhone away from an outlet. The flat form factor of the IMP70D makes this possible. With the port end facing up in the zippered pocket, the ON button is easily accessed being on the side of the unit next to the USB ports at one corner of the unit - I don't have to unzip a pocket to press it or fumble around trying to access it. If I had to, I could simultaneously charge the iPad and the iPhone while both rested in my vest.

With all the electronic devices, wiring and battery I now wear in my vest, I might have to start being concerned that someone will mistake me for a suicide bomber!
